properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 30 at 12:39AM CDT until August 30 at 1:45AM CDT by NWS Aberdeen SD
properties.description:
SVRABR

The National Weather Service in Aberdeen has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northeastern Sully County in central South Dakota...
East Central Dewey County in north central South Dakota...
Potter County in north central South Dakota...

* Until 145 AM CDT /1245 AM MDT/.

* At 1239 AM CDT /1139 PM MDT/, a severe thunderstorm was located
over Whitlocks Bay Rec Area, or 13 miles west of Gettysburg, moving
east at 25 mph.

THIS IS A DESTRUCTIVE STORM FOR SOUTHEAST POTTER COUNTY.

HAZARD...Three inch hail and 60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be severely injured.
Expect shattered windows, extensive damage to roofs,
siding, and vehicles.

* This severe thunderstorm will be near...
Whitlocks Bay Rec Area and Swiftbird around 1240 AM CDT.
Gorman around 1250 AM CDT.
Gettysburg around 110 AM CDT.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter now inside an interior room on the lowest floor of a
well-built structure. This storm is capable of producing destructive
hail and damaging winds.

Report severe weather to your nearest law enforcement agency or the
National Weather Service office in Aberdeen SD.
properties.area: Dewey, SD; Potter, SD; Sully, SD

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued August 30 at 12:32AM CDT by NWS Bismarck ND
properties.description:
At 1132 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 15
miles south of New England, or 23 miles northeast of Bowman, moving
northeast at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Mainly rural areas of Southeastern Slope and West Central Hettinger
Counties.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued August 29 at 10:27PM MST until August 30 at 12:45AM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
FFWTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Western Graham County in southeastern Arizona...
East Central Pinal County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 1245 AM MST.

* At 1027 PM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms produced heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1
and 3 inches of rain have fallen in the Aravaipa Watershed.
Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected. A stream gauge in the Aravaipa Canyon showed a rapid 6
foot rise and this flood wave is moving downstream. Hikers and
campers should move away from the creek now.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Aravaipa Canyon Wilderness.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Deer Creek, Telegraph Wash and Aravaipa Creek.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Central Pima County in southeastern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 930 AM MST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Rises in small streams and normally dry washes. Overflowing poor
drainage areas. Some low-water crossings may become impassable.

thunderstorms fell in the middle and upper reaches of the Vamori
Wash this evening. This will cause small stream flooding. Rises
in the Vamori Wash could be sudden, but the flood wave will
slowly travel downstream.

San Simon Wash, Hali Murk Wash, Chukut Kuk Wash, San Luis Wash
and Vamori Wash.

Santa Cruz and Kupk.

properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...the Colorado River near
mile marker 62.

* Until 1215 AM MST /115 AM MDT/ Tonight.

* At 522 PM MST /622 PM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
that produced heavy rain earlier southwest of Cameron have resulted
in a flash flood along the Little Colorado River west of Cameron.
Between 1 and 2 inches were estimate by radar earlier in the
afternoon. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
The flood wave is expected to reach the Colorado River between 10
PM and 1 AM.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain from
thunderstorms earlier.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding along the Little Colorado
River west of Cameron.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Little Colorado River Navajo Tribal Park.

This includes the following highways...
the Colorado River near mile marker 62. State Route 64 between mile
markers 281 and 284.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Blue Water Base Camp, Old Fish Camp Site, Above LCR Camp Site and
Below LCR Camp Site.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Blue Water Base Camp.

This includes the following Little Colorado River west of Cameron.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 29 at 5:29PM CDT until August 31 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Indianapolis IN
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following river in Illinois...
Indiana...

Wabash River at Hutsonville to Vincennes

.Minor flooding continues on the Wabash River from Hutsonville down
to Vincennes. The river has crested. Flooding should come to an end
on the Wabash over the weekend.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River at Riverton.

* WHEN...Until Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, Extensive lowland flooding is in progress.
High water surrounds many river cabins.  Access to most river
cabins is by boat only.  Levees begin to protect farmland.
Extensive flooding of Leaverton Park occurs in Palestine, Illinois.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:00 PM CDT /6:00 PM EDT/ Saturday the stage was 17.6 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 5:00 PM CDT /6:00 PM EDT/ Saturday was 19.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
Monday morning and continue falling to 5.1 feet Tuesday,
September 08.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 915 AM CDT /1015
AM EDT/.
